before: An iterator supplies values through next(), which returns a record with value and done.

after:
An iterator gives values one at a time. Call its `next()` method to ask for the next result.

The result has a `value` and a `done` flag. `done: true` means the sequence has finished.

A generator is a convenient way to make an iterator. Write its function with `function*`.

Calling the function creates a generator object. Its body waits until a value is requested.

The next call to `next()` resumes just after the previous `yield`.

After the function finishes, `next()` reports `done: true`. The finished generator has no more values to give.

`for...of` can request values from a generator until it finishes. Spread, such as `[...generator]`, collects them into an array.

Only collect a sequence that ends. An endless generator would never finish spreading.

Each call to the generator function makes a new sequence with its own position.

Using a finished generator again does not restart it. Call the function again for a fresh one.

Complete `positiveSteps(n)` so it yields the numbers from 1 through `n`, one at a time.

The input is a whole number that is zero or greater. For zero, yield nothing. Use a loop and `yield`, without building an array first.
